title: United Nations Young Professionals Programme (YPP): Eligibility, Application Process, Exam Guide and How to Prepare
summary: Dreaming of an international career with purpose? The United Nations Young Professionals Programme (YPP) offers talented and highly qualified young professionals an opportunity to begin a career as an international civil servant with the United Nations Secretariat. 🌍🇺🇳 Applications are expected to open in mid-October — but you do not need to wait until applications open to start preparing. If you are considering applying, now is the time to check your eligibility, understand the application requirements and begin preparing for the YPP examination. Read on to learn about the UN YPP, eligibility requirements, application process, examination stages and how to prepare. What Is the United Nations Young Professionals Programme (YPP)? Young Professionals Programme The UN Young Professionals Programme (YPP) is a recruitment initiative for talented, highly qualified professionals to start a career as an international civil servant with the UN Secretariat. It consists of an entrance examination process and professional development once those who are successful start their career with the UN. The YPP examination is held once a year in different subject areas, depending on the needs of the UN. YPP is open to nationals of participating countries. The list of participating countries varies from year to year. The application period typically opens in June each year. Applications Open Mid-October — Start Preparing Now If you are interested in applying for the YPP, do not wait until the application window opens to begin preparing . Applications are expected to open in mid-October , making this the ideal time to: Check whether your country is participating. Confirm that you meet the age and education requirements. Check your English or French language proficiency. Review the YPP application requirements. Gather your degree and identification documents. Update your CV and employment information. Familiarise yourself with the examination format. Begin reviewing relevant preparation materials. Make sure you understand the subject area for the upcoming examination. The application process itself is only one part of the journey. Candidates should also allow enough time to prepare for the competitive YPP examination. Start preparing now so that you are ready when applications open. Who Can Apply for the UN Young Professionals Programme? To be eligible for the YPP, candidates generally need to meet the following requirements. 1. Nationality You must be a national of a participating United Nations Member State . The participating countries are not necessarily the same every year, so applicants should check the official YPP announcement for the relevant examination cycle. 2. Education You must have at least a first-level university degree relevant to the examination subject area. This generally means having a relevant Bachelor s degree or a three-year equivalent first university degree. 3. Age Candidates must be 32 years old or younger in the year of the examination . The specific birth-date requirement should always be checked against the official announcement for the relevant YPP cycle. 4. Language Candidates must be fluent in English or French , which are the two working languages used for the YPP examination. How to Apply for the UN YPP YPP applications are submitted online through the United Nations recruitment system, Inspira . Before applying, candidates should: Confirm that their nationality is included among the participating countries. Check the age requirement. Confirm that their university degree is relevant to the examination subject. Confirm their English or French language proficiency. Review the specific YPP job opening. Prepare the required documentation. Complete and submit the online application before the deadline. Applications are normally submitted through the relevant YPP job opening on the UN Careers/Inspira platform. What Happens After You Apply? Applications are screened to determine whether candidates meet the basic eligibility requirements. The screening process considers factors including: Nationality Age Education Language proficiency If there are more than 90 eligible applicants from the same country for a particular examination area, additional criteria may be used to rank candidates. These can include: Highest level of education Knowledge of additional official UN languages Relevant professional experience Where the examination has two stages, candidates may be selected for the first stage based on this ranking, with a smaller number progressing to the second stage. Applicants are informed of the outcome of the screening process. UN YPP Application Timeline *The timeline can change from year to year. For the upcoming application cycle, candidates should prepare ahead of the expected mid-October opening rather than waiting until applications go live. How to Prepare for the UN YPP Application Preparation should begin before the application deadline. Check your eligibility early Do not leave it until the last minute to discover that you do not meet an eligibility requirement. Check: Your nationality Your age Your degree Your language proficiency The examination subject area Prepare your documents You may need documentation confirming your identity, nationality and education. Make sure your documents are available and that the information in your application is accurate and consistent. Review your education information When completing your application, provide accurate information about your university degree. If there are differences between your degree and the terminology used in the application system, use the appropriate section to explain them rather than selecting an inaccurate option. Check your language proficiency carefully Language proficiency is important. Candidates must demonstrate fluency in either English or French. The UN application process considers speaking, reading, writing and understanding. Anything below the required level of fluency in one of these areas can affect eligibility. What Is the UN YPP Examination Like? The YPP examination normally consists of an online examination, often conducted in two stages, followed by an interview for candidates who progress through the process. Candidates can use the UN s examination preparation resources to familiarise themselves with the format and expectations. Preparation materials can include: Reading lists Sample questions Previous examination questions Examination tips and guidance Stage One: General and Specialized Questions The first stage normally consists of multiple-choice questions covering both: General assessment This may assess areas such as: Written communication Reasoning UN core values UN competencies Specialized assessment This focuses on knowledge relevant to the specific YPP examination subject area. The first stage generally lasts around two hours and is conducted in English or French. Stage Two: Specialized Examination Candidates who progress to the second stage may complete a more detailed specialized examination. This stage can include constructed or open-ended questions related to the examination subject. The examination generally lasts approximately two to two and a half hours . Some questions may allow candidates to respond in one of the six official UN languages, depending on the examination requirements. Candidates should pay close attention to: Question instructions Word limits Time management The specific requirements of each question The examination may also be remotely proctored. YPP Interview Candidates who successfully progress through the examination stages may be invited to a competency-based interview , generally conducted by video conference. The interview provides an opportunity to demonstrate relevant competencies and suitability for a career with the United Nations. Candidates should therefore prepare examples that demonstrate their skills, experience, judgement and ability to work effectively in an international environment. How Competitive Is the UN YPP? The YPP is a competitive recruitment programme. The number of candidates who can progress through the screening and examination stages may depend on the number of eligible applicants from each participating country and the examination subject area. This makes early preparation particularly important. Being eligible does not guarantee selection , and passing an examination does not automatically mean that a candidate will be offered a position. What Happens If You Pass the YPP Examination? Successful candidates may be placed on a YPP roster for suitable vacancies. The roster is generally valid for three years . However, being placed on the roster does not guarantee employment with the United Nations. Candidates selected for positions may be offered a two-year fixed-term appointment , with the possibility of continuing employment subject to satisfactory performance and applicable UN policies. What Grade Do YPP Candidates Receive? Depending on their qualifications and experience, successful candidates may enter at the: P-1 level Generally applicable to candidates with a Bachelor s degree and no relevant professional work experience. P-2 level Generally applicable to candidates with: A Bachelor s degree and two years of relevant work experience, or A Master s degree and no relevant work experience. Candidates are generally expected to spend at least two years in their first position. Where Can UN YPP Candidates Be Posted? YPP professionals may be assigned to different United Nations duty stations depending on organisational needs. Possible locations include: Addis Ababa Bangkok Beirut Geneva Nairobi New York Santiago Vienna Candidates should be prepared to serve at different duty stations and, where applicable, in field operations. Managed Reassignment Programme After serving in their initial position for at least two years, eligible staff may participate in the Managed Reassignment Programme . The programme is intended to support professional development, diversify staff experience and help employees develop skills through different assignments. Upcoming UN YPP Examination Subject The examination subject area changes according to the staffing needs of the United Nations. For the relevant cycle, applicants should carefully review the official YPP announcement to confirm: The examination subject Participating countries Eligibility requirements Application dates Examination dates Required qualifications This information can change from one cycle to another. UN Staff and the Young Professionals Programme Current United Nations staff may also be eligible to participate in the YPP under specific internal arrangements. Staff members in General Service and related categories, as well as certain Field Service staff, may be eligible depending on their grade, appointment, nationality, qualifications, performance and other requirements. There are also specific provisions for internal candidates progressing from General Service positions to professional positions. Employees interested in this route should check the relevant internal YPP vacancy and eligibility requirements in Inspira. Check the official UN YPP information and prepare ahead of the application opening. Beware of Companies Charging for YPP Applications Applicants should be cautious of companies that charge fees for YPP-related services. The United Nations has stated that it does not collaborate or partner with for-profit companies offering YPP application or examination services . There are no fees for submitting a YPP application, taking the examination or undergoing the evaluation process . Candidates can access official information and preparation materials publicly and free of charge. Frequently Asked Questions About the UN YPP When will UN YPP applications open? Applications for the upcoming cycle are expected to open in mid-October . Candidates should monitor the official UN Careers/Inspira announcement for the exact opening and closing dates. Can I start preparing before applications open? Yes — and you should. Use the period before applications open to check your eligibility, gather your documents, understand the examination format and begin studying the relevant subject area. What age do I need to be? Candidates generally need to be 32 years old or younger in the year of the examination . Always check the exact requirement in the official announcement. Do I need a Master s degree? No. A relevant first-level university degree , such as a Bachelor s degree or equivalent, can meet the education requirement. Do I need work experience? Work experience is not necessarily an eligibility requirement. However, relevant professional experience can be considered when ranking candidates where there are large numbers of eligible applicants. Which languages are accepted? Candidates must generally be fluent in English or French . Is the YPP examination difficult? The YPP is competitive and requires preparation. Candidates should become familiar with the examination structure, review relevant materials and practise answering questions under time constraints. Does passing YPP guarantee a UN job? No. Successful candidates may be placed on a roster, but roster placement does not guarantee employment. Is there a fee to apply? No. The United Nations does not charge an application or examination fee for the YPP. Final Advice: Start Preparing Now If you have been dreaming of an international career with purpose , the UN Young Professionals Programme could be an opportunity worth exploring. With applications expected to open in mid-October , now is the time to prepare. Don t wait until the application portal opens. ✅ Check your eligibility ✅ Confirm your nationality and age requirements ✅ Review your degree qualifications ✅ Prepare your supporting documents ✅ Check your English or French proficiency ✅ Learn how the YPP examination works ✅ Review the available preparation materials ✅ Start preparing for the examination The application may open in October, but your preparation can start today. 🌍🇺🇳 Check the official UN YPP information and prepare ahead of the application opening. Those interested can apply via Inspira. To learn more, read the information below, check out our curated series of informative videos about YPP , and continue to visit Important Updates to stay informed! Applicants should always consult the latest official UN announcement for the current application cycle, as participating countries, examination subjects, dates and requirements can change. title: Collective Mind Collaboration Fellows 2026–2027: Apply for a Global Co-Creation Fellowship
summary: Are you an experienced practitioner working with networks, coalitions, alliances, partnerships or other collaborative organisations ? Collective Mind is inviting practitioners from around the world to become Collective Mind Collaboration Fellows and help co-create a new AI-powered collaboration tool. The Collective Mind Collaboration Fellows programme 2026–2027 is a year-long opportunity for experienced professionals and practitioners to contribute their knowledge, connect with a global community, influence the development of a new digital tool, and gain free access to the Collective Mind Compass . Applications are being reviewed on a rolling basis , with the final deadline to participate set for 30 November 2026 . Key Details: Collective Mind Collaboration Fellows 2026–2027 Opportunity Collective Mind Collaboration Fellows Organisation Collective Mind Programme Collaboration Fellows Duration One year Phase 1 September 2026 – February 2027 Phase 2 March – August 2027 Location Global / Worldwide Who can apply Experienced collaboration practitioners Focus areas Strategy, resource mobilisation, MEL and collaboration Free Compass access Six months from launch Compass launch February 2027 Application deadline 30 November 2026 Applications Rolling basis About Collaboration Fellows Collaboration Fellows are experienced practitioners anywhere in the world who are working in or alongside networks, coalitions, alliances, partnerships, or other collaborative organizations. The fellowship is a year-long program in two phases: Co-Creation (September 2026 February 2027) During the first phase, Fellows contribute to the knowledge base of our Compass by capturing and sharing their experiences – especially about strategy, resource mobilization, and monitoring, evaluation, and learning – using the templates and tools we provide (e.g., case studies, interviews, guided workflows, etc.). To be eligible for the second phase, fellows must make at least two contributions during the first Co-Creation phase. Community Building (March August 2027) During the second phase, Fellows gain free access to the Compass, engaging with each other, with our experts, and with other users. Over the course of the fellowship, fellows will also have opportunities to weigh in on development decisions in meaningful ways, sharing their feedback and ideas on the tool’s design, rollout, and ongoing improvements. Collaboration Fellows receive multiple benefits: Access: 6 months of free access to the Compass from its launch in February, plus opportunities to extend your access via referrals. Learning and support: Access to resources available on the platform, including the AI coaches, discussions, events, and more. Visibility: Named as a contributor to the tool. Recognition: Contributions may be published, shared, and promoted via Collective Mind’s channels (website, newsletter, LinkedIn). Promotion: Opportunities to be highlighted as an expert, such as during discussions and events. Connections: Connections to diverse global practitioners, including other fellows and Collective Mind’s Co-Creators. Community: Relationship-building via a dedicated shared space for fellows on the platform and fellows-only calls and events. Collaboration Fellows will also be considered fellows for life, with ongoing opportunities and connection to Collective Mind. Apply to become a Collective Mind Collaboration Fellow Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The deadline to participate is November 30th . A Fellowship That Continues Beyond 2027 One distinctive feature of the programme is that Collaboration Fellows will be considered fellows for life . This means participants can remain connected to Collective Mind and potentially benefit from future opportunities, relationships and activities beyond the formal year-long fellowship. The programme therefore offers more than temporary access to a digital platform. It provides an opportunity to become part of a long-term global community of collaboration practitioners . How to Apply for the Collective Mind Collaboration Fellows Programme Interested practitioners are encouraged to apply to join the Collective Mind co-creation effort. Application deadline: 30 November 2026 Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis , so prospective applicants are encouraged to apply early rather than waiting until the deadline. Apply to become a Collective Mind Collaboration Fellow You can also learn more about the Collective Mind Compass and the co-creation initiative through Collective Mind s official website. Why Apply? The Collective Mind Collaboration Fellows programme offers experienced practitioners a chance to shape an emerging AI-powered collaboration tool while sharing their expertise and building connections with a global community . For professionals working in networks, coalitions, partnerships and collective action, the fellowship could provide a valuable opportunity to contribute practical knowledge, gain visibility, access new learning resources and influence the development of a tool designed to improve collaboration. Applications are open now and will be reviewed on a rolling basis until 30 November 2026. title: Constellation Energy 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Internship: Paid Remote Opportunity for Environmental Science and Sustainability Students
summary: Constellation is inviting applications for its 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Intern position, a paid internship designed for university students interested in sustainability, environmental science, business, climate strategy, and the future of clean and reliable energy. The internship offers students an opportunity to gain practical, hands-on experience with Constellation’s Sustainability Team while contributing to projects connected to sustainability and climate strategy. The position is structured as a remote internship and will run for approximately 10 weeks during the summer of 2027. For students looking to build professional experience in sustainability, environmental management, climate strategy, clean energy, corporate sustainability, or related areas, this internship provides an opportunity to develop practical skills while working under the supervision of experienced professionals. About Constellation Constellation is a major energy company focused on producing clean and reliable electricity and supporting the transition toward a cleaner energy future. The company describes itself as the largest private-sector power producer in the world and the largest producer of clean and reliable energy in the United States. Following its integration with Calpine, Constellation s portfolio includes approximately 55 gigawatts of generating capacity across a range of energy sources, including: Nuclear power Natural gas Geothermal energy Hydroelectric power Wind energy Solar energy According to the opportunity description, this generating capacity is enough to power the equivalent of approximately 27 million homes . Constellation says its work is guided by a purpose of helping create a cleaner planet and healthier communities while meeting the energy needs of today and tomorrow. The company s workplace emphasizes professional growth, learning, collaboration, and meaningful contributions. For interns, this environment can provide exposure to the practical challenges organizations face when developing and implementing sustainability strategies within the energy sector. About the 2027 Sustainability and Climate Strategy Internship The 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Intern position is intended for highly motivated students pursuing undergraduate or graduate degrees in fields such as Environmental Science, Sustainability, Business Administration, or related disciplines. The internship is with Constellation s Sustainability Team and is designed around specific projects that allow interns to gain real-world experience. Rather than being limited to classroom-based learning, interns will have the opportunity to work on practical assignments under the guidance of an assigned supervisor. This structure can help students understand how sustainability and climate-related concepts are applied in a large energy organization. The position is listed as: Position: 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Intern Company: Constellation Department/Team: Sustainability Team Job Type: Intern Work Arrangement: Remote Location Listed: Baltimore, Maryland, USA Job Number: 138731 Internship Period: June 7, 2027 to August 13, 2027 Duration: Approximately 10 weeks Compensation: Paid internship What Interns Can Expect The internship is designed to provide students with hands-on professional experience. Interns will be assigned specific projects and will work independently while receiving supervision and guidance. This type of internship can be particularly valuable for students who want to understand how sustainability functions within a major energy organization. Through their project work, interns may have opportunities to develop or strengthen skills such as: Sustainability analysis Climate strategy Environmental research Business analysis Problem-solving Written communication Verbal communication Team collaboration Project work Independent working Analytical thinking Creative thinking Professional interpersonal skills The position also emphasizes the ability to contribute within a team-oriented environment while independently handling assigned responsibilities. Internship Dates and Duration The 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Internship is expected to run for approximately 10 weeks . The scheduled internship period is: June 7, 2027 – August 13, 2027 Students considering applying should ensure that they can participate during the stated internship period. Because the position is specifically described as a summer internship, applicants should also consider how the dates fit with their academic calendar and other commitments. Educational Requirements Applicants must currently be pursuing a Bachelor s or Master s degree . The preferred areas of study include: Environmental Science Sustainability Business Administration Related fields Students whose academic programs combine sustainability, environmental studies, climate, business, energy, environmental policy, or other closely related disciplines may find the opportunity particularly relevant. The requirement to be currently pursuing a degree means the position is targeted toward students rather than applicants who have already completed their education and are seeking a conventional full-time position. Academic Requirements Applicants are required to meet specific academic standards. Constellation lists the following minimum GPA requirements: 2.8 cumulative GPA 3.0 major GPA In addition to meeting the stated GPA thresholds, candidates should demonstrate a strong overall record of academic performance. The company specifically seeks candidates with a track record of outstanding academic performance , meaning applicants should be prepared to demonstrate their academic strengths through their application materials. Students should therefore ensure that their resumes and other application materials accurately present their educational background, academic achievements, relevant coursework, projects, research, or other accomplishments that demonstrate their preparation for the internship. Skills and Personal Qualities Constellation Is Seeking Academic qualifications are only one part of the selection criteria. Constellation is also looking for students who can contribute effectively in a professional environment. Teamwork and Collaboration Successful interns are expected to be comfortable working in a team-oriented environment. Sustainability and climate strategy projects often involve collaboration between people with different professional backgrounds, so applicants should demonstrate an ability to work effectively with others. Creative and Analytical Thinking The internship requires the ability to work both creatively and analytically in a problem-solving environment. Applicants should therefore be able to approach challenges from different perspectives, analyze information carefully, identify potential solutions, and contribute practical ideas. Leadership Constellation also highlights leadership skills among the qualities it seeks. Students do not necessarily need extensive professional management experience; leadership can also be demonstrated through university projects, student organizations, volunteer activities, research, community initiatives, or other experiences where the applicant took responsibility and helped achieve a goal. Communication Skills Strong communication is another important requirement. Applicants should possess: Excellent written communication skills Excellent verbal communication skills Strong interpersonal skills These abilities are particularly important in a remote working environment, where clear written and verbal communication can help teams coordinate projects and maintain productivity. Remote Work Opportunity One of the notable features of this internship is its remote work arrangement . The position is listed as remote, allowing successful interns to undertake their assigned work without being required to work physically from Constellation s Baltimore location. However, applicants should carefully review the company s employment eligibility requirements before applying. The fact that the internship is remote does not mean it is open to applicants worldwide. U.S. Work Authorization Requirement A particularly important requirement for international applicants is Constellation s visa policy. The company explicitly states that it will not provide visa sponsorship for this position now or in the future . Applicants must therefore have the legal ability to work in the United States without requiring either current or future visa sponsorship. This is an important consideration for international students and candidates living outside the United States. Simply meeting the educational and GPA requirements does not make an applicant eligible if they cannot legally work in the United States under the conditions specified by Constellation. Prospective applicants should carefully assess their own U.S. work authorization status before submitting an application. Equal Employment Opportunity Constellation states that it is an equal opportunity employer. According to the employer, applicants and employees are considered without regard to characteristics including: Age Color Disability Gender National origin Race Religion Sexual orientation Gender identity Veteran status Other classifications protected under applicable federal, state, or local law This means the company states that employment decisions are made in accordance with applicable equal employment opportunity requirements. Constellation also says it is committed to attracting, retaining, and advancing employees who can serve its customers, partners, and communities while maintaining a workplace based on mutual respect and opportunities for professional growth. Disability and Interview Accommodations Applicants who have a disability, whether visible or invisible, and require an accommodation to complete the application process can contact Constellation s Talent Acquisition team using the accommodation contact provided in the original listing. Candidates who require an interview accommodation can also use the company s interview accommodation resources. Applicants should request accommodations through the appropriate company channel if they need assistance during the recruitment process. Nuclear Site Access and Identification Requirements Constellation notes that many of its roles may require unescorted entry and access to nuclear sites at the time of hire and during employment. The company states that, beginning May 7, 2025, candidates requiring unescorted access to applicable nuclear sites need an acceptable form of identification in accordance with the REAL ID Act. The identification options listed include: REAL ID Passport Visa TWIC Card This requirement may not necessarily apply to every intern or to a fully remote position, but applicants should be aware that Constellation operates nuclear facilities and that certain roles may involve additional access requirements. Why This Internship Could Be Valuable The Constellation Sustainability and Climate Strategy Internship can be valuable for students seeking to establish a career in the growing sustainability and clean-energy sector. 1. Paid Professional Experience The internship is a paid summer opportunity, allowing students to gain professional experience while receiving compensation. 2. Experience With a Major Energy Company Working with a large energy organization can expose students to the scale and complexity of sustainability challenges within the power sector. 3. Hands-On Project Experience Interns will work on specific projects rather than simply observing the Sustainability Team. This can help them build practical experience that may strengthen future applications for graduate programs, internships, fellowships, and entry-level sustainability positions. 4. Remote Working Experience The remote structure can help students develop the communication, organization, independence, and collaboration skills required in modern professional workplaces. 5. Sustainability and Climate Exposure Students interested in sustainability, climate strategy, environmental issues, and energy transition can gain exposure to these subjects within a major energy organization. 6. Professional Development Working under an assigned supervisor can give interns the opportunity to receive guidance while learning how professional teams plan, execute, and deliver projects. How to Prepare a Strong Application Students interested in this opportunity should make sure their application clearly demonstrates both their academic qualifications and relevant skills. A strong application should emphasize: Current degree program: Clearly state the degree being pursued and the institution. Relevant academic field: Highlight Environmental Science, Sustainability, Business Administration, or another related discipline. GPA: Make sure the application reflects the required cumulative and major GPA where appropriate. Relevant coursework: Include courses connected to sustainability, environmental management, climate, business, energy, data analysis, or related subjects. Projects: Highlight university, research, community, or personal projects relevant to sustainability or climate strategy. Communication: Demonstrate strong written and verbal communication abilities. Problem-solving: Provide examples of analytical or creative approaches used to solve problems. Leadership: Mention experiences where you led or took responsibility for a project or activity. Teamwork: Highlight successful collaboration with classmates, colleagues, organizations, or project teams. Remote-work readiness: Where relevant, demonstrate your ability to work independently, manage deadlines, and communicate effectively in a remote environment. Applicants should also carefully review their resume for spelling, formatting, consistency, and relevance before submitting it. Who Should Apply? This opportunity is particularly suited to students who are currently pursuing a Bachelor s or Master s degree in: Environmental Science Sustainability Business Administration A related field Applicants should also meet the required GPA thresholds, demonstrate strong academic performance, possess effective communication and interpersonal skills, and be capable of contributing creatively and analytically to problem-solving activities. The internship may be especially relevant to students planning careers in: Sustainability Climate strategy Environmental management Clean energy Energy policy Corporate sustainability Environmental consulting Sustainable business Climate risk Energy transition Environmental research APPLY HERE Geographic and Nationality Eligibility Although the internship is remote , it is not presented as a worldwide remote opportunity. Constellation requires applicants to have the ability to lawfully work in the United States without current or future visa sponsorship . Therefore, applicants from outside the United States should not assume that they are eligible simply because the position is remote. Eligibility depends on the applicant s existing legal authorization to work in the United States and the employer s stated sponsorship policy. Constellation s equal opportunity statement also indicates that employment consideration is not restricted on the basis of race, national origin, or other protected characteristics. However, the U.S. work authorization requirement remains applicable. Visit HERE to learn more about the Constellation Energy 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Internship. Application Process Interested candidates should apply through Constellation s official careers/application system. Applicants should prepare their application carefully and make sure that all information provided is accurate. Particular attention should be given to degree status, field of study, GPA, work authorization, and relevant academic or professional experience. Candidates should also be cautious about recruitment scams and rely on Constellation s official careers channels when submitting personal information or application materials. Deadline No specific application deadline is stated in the provided job listing. Because the position is for Summer 2027, interested students should consider applying as early as possible rather than waiting for a deadline to be announced or for the position to close. Key Details at a Glance Opportunity: 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Intern Organization: Constellation Opportunity Type: Paid internship Work Arrangement: Remote Listed Location: Baltimore, Maryland, USA Internship Duration: Approximately 10 weeks Start Date: June 7, 2027 End Date: August 13, 2027 Eligible Education: Students pursuing Bachelor s or Master s degrees Preferred Fields: Environmental Science, Sustainability, Business Administration, or related fields Minimum Cumulative GPA: 2.8 Minimum Major GPA: 3.0 Work Authorization: Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future visa sponsorship Visa Sponsorship: Not provided Application Deadline: Not specified in the provided listing Conclusion The Constellation 2027 Summer Sustainability and Climate Strategy Internship presents a valuable opportunity for students who want to gain practical experience at the intersection of sustainability, climate strategy, business, and the energy sector. The approximately 10-week paid internship is structured around hands-on projects within Constellation s Sustainability Team, giving successful candidates an opportunity to develop professional skills while working under an assigned supervisor. The position particularly targets students pursuing Bachelor s or Master s degrees in Environmental Science, Sustainability, Business Administration, and related disciplines. Applicants should pay close attention to the 2.8 cumulative GPA and 3.0 major GPA requirements , as well as the requirement to be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future visa sponsorship. title: Women in Foreign Affairs Mentorship Group 2026 with Alyse Nelson: Applications Open for Women in Foreign Affairs
summary: Women pursuing careers in diplomacy, international relations, foreign policy, security, human rights, global development, and other related areas have an opportunity to join the Women in Foreign Affairs Network Mentorship Group , an initiative designed to create a supportive and inclusive environment where women can learn from experienced leaders in foreign affairs. The 16th Cohort of the Women in Foreign Affairs Network Mentorship Group will be led by Alyse Nelson , President, CEO, and Co-Founder of Vital Voices Global Partnership. The mentorship group will provide participants with an opportunity to engage in three monthly, off-the-record group coaching sessions focused on leadership, decision-making, navigating professional challenges, and gaining behind-the-scenes insights into the foreign policy field. Applications for the 2026 mentorship group are currently open, with applications due by October 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM EST . About the Women in Foreign Affairs Mentorship Group The Women in Foreign Affairs Network Mentorship Group seeks to bring together women from diverse professional and personal backgrounds who share an interest in foreign affairs and want to learn from established women leaders. The program is designed around the idea that women working in foreign policy and international affairs can benefit significantly from a supportive professional community. Participants will have the opportunity to learn directly from prominent leaders while also connecting with other women navigating careers in the field. Rather than focusing solely on formal instruction, the mentorship group emphasizes practical insights and candid conversations. The sessions are held off the record, creating an environment where participants can engage openly and discuss issues that may not typically be addressed in public professional settings. The mentorship group is intended to help women better understand the realities of leadership and professional advancement in foreign affairs while developing relationships with peers and senior figures in the field. What Participants Can Expect Selected participants will take part in three monthly group coaching sessions led by the cohort s mentor. Each mentor is responsible for selecting a particular theme and guiding participants through a series of three sessions focused on that theme. The sessions are intended to provide practical and behind-the-scenes perspectives on leadership and professional development. Participants can expect discussions covering areas such as Challenges commonly faced by women in the foreign policy and foreign affairs sector. Leadership approaches and decision-making processes. Professional challenges and how experienced leaders navigate them. Blind spots and structural challenges within the foreign affairs field. Career decision-making and professional growth. Leadership development and building confidence. Perspectives gained from years of experience in international affairs. Building relationships with other women working across the foreign affairs ecosystem. The off-the-record format is particularly important because it is intended to provide a safe environment for participants to ask questions, share experiences, and engage in honest discussions. Attendance Requirement Participation in the mentorship group requires a meaningful commitment from selected candidates. The organizers have stated that at least two of the three sessions are mandatory . Applicants must therefore confirm that they are available for the scheduled sessions before applying. The three sessions are scheduled as follows: Session 1 Date: October 15, 2026 Time: 7:00–8:00 PM CEST / 1:00–2:00 PM EST Session 2 Date: November 6, 2026 Time: 7:00–8:00 PM CEST / 1:00–2:00 PM EST Session 3 Date: December 9, 2026 Time: 8:00–9:00 PM CEST / 2:00–3:00 PM EST Applicants must confirm their availability and understand that they are required to attend at least two of these meetings. The program aims to make the sector more accessible by providing women with opportunities to learn directly from experienced professionals and understand how careers in foreign affairs develop. 3. This mentorship group goes further by creating opportunities to learn about the practical realities of leadership. Participants can gain insights into how experienced leaders approach difficult decisions, navigate professional challenges, and develop their careers. 4. Creating a Safe Space for Career Conversations The network seeks to provide an environment where women can support one another in making professional and career decisions. Her extensive experience makes the Q4 2026 mentorship group particularly relevant for women seeking practical perspectives on leadership, foreign policy, international affairs, and advancing women s participation in global decision-making. The program is therefore potentially relevant to women who have already established careers as well as those who are at earlier stages of their professional development. Applicants may have backgrounds or professional interests connected to areas such as: Diplomacy. Security and defense policy. Human rights and humanitarian issues. International law. Global environmental and climate policy. Global economic policy. Global health policy. Global gender policy. Technology and foreign policy. Regional specialization. Other areas related to foreign affairs. The application allows candidates to select up to three areas of expertise or provide another relevant area under the Other option. Areas of Expertise Covered in the Application Applicants are asked to identify their area of expertise. Global Environmental and Climate Policy This area is relevant to professionals working on climate change, environmental policy, sustainability, natural resources, or international environmental governance. Global Economic Policy Applicants working on international economics, trade, development finance, economic policy, global markets, or related fields may select this category. Global Health Policy Professionals working on international health, global health governance, health policy, health security, or related issues may select global health policy. Global Gender Policy This category may be particularly relevant to applicants working on gender equality, women s empowerment, women s political participation, gender policy, or related international issues. Technology and Foreign Policy Applicants working at the intersection of technology and international affairs can identify this as their area of expertise. Regional Specialization Candidates with professional or academic expertise focused on a particular geographical region can select regional specialization. Other Applicants whose expertise does not fall into the listed categories may specify another relevant area. Application Requirements The application requires candidates to provide several pieces of personal and professional information. Applicants will be asked to provide: Full name Email address LinkedIn profile City of residence for the next six months Area of expertise Background and explanation of why the program matters to them Additional information they would like the organizers to know Confirmation of availability for the mentorship sessions The application includes a 250-word maximum for the question asking candidates to explain their background and why the program matters to them. How to Prepare a Strong Application Because the mentorship group is likely to receive more applications than available places, candidates should make their application focused and compelling. Applicants should consider highlighting: Their professional experience in foreign affairs or a related field. Their academic background and relevant areas of study. Their specific interest in international affairs. The challenges they have encountered in their career. Their leadership ambitions. How mentorship would contribute to their professional development. Why learning from an experienced foreign affairs leader would be valuable to them. What perspectives or experiences they could contribute to the mentorship community. Their commitment to supporting other women in the field. The 250-word response should not simply repeat information from a CV. Instead, applicants should use the limited space to tell a clear professional story and explain why participation in the mentorship group is important at this stage of their career. title: Field Studies Council Youth Panel 2026: Join the UK-Wide Youth Environmental Leadership Panel
summary: Applications are now open for the Field Studies Council Youth Panel 2026 , an exciting opportunity for young people in the United Kingdom to contribute their ideas, experiences and perspectives to one of the UK’s leading environmental education charities. The Youth Panel brings together young people who are passionate about nature, the outdoors and environmental education. Panel members have the opportunity to influence how the Field Studies Council engages with young people, participate in discussions with staff and trustees, develop valuable transferable skills, meet other young naturalists and environmentalists, and contribute to content and projects focused on youth engagement. Applications opened on 14 September 2026 , and eligible young people are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline of 9:00 pm on Sunday, 27 September 2026 . About the Field Studies Council Youth Panel The Field Studies Council Youth Panel is a UK-wide group of young people that helps shape nature education and youth engagement through strategic insight and feedback. Youth Panel members play an important role within the Field Studies Council by bringing young people s perspectives into organisational discussions. Rather than simply participating in environmental activities, members can contribute their views on how young people can be better engaged with nature, outdoor learning and environmental education. The opportunity is particularly suitable for young people who want to become a stronger voice for their generation while gaining practical experience in communication, decision-making, teamwork and influencing. The role is voluntary, meaning that successful applicants will not be employed or paid as Youth Panel members. However, the position provides opportunities for personal development, networking, training and involvement in the work of the Field Studies Council. What Does a Youth Panel Member Do? Youth Panel members are expected to actively contribute to the Panel and participate in activities that support the Field Studies Council s youth engagement work. The Panel provides young people with an opportunity to have their voices heard in discussions concerning the organisation s provision for young people. Members can provide feedback, share ideas, participate in meetings and contribute to projects based on their interests and skills. The Field Studies Council describes its Youth Panel members as key members of the organisation who can engage in high-level discussions about its provision for young people. This makes the opportunity particularly valuable for young people interested in: Environmental education Nature and conservation Youth engagement Environmental leadership Communication and content creation Decision-making Advocacy and representation Biodiversity Outdoor learning Community engagement Developing leadership and teamwork skills Key Benefits of Joining the Youth Panel Being selected for the Field Studies Council Youth Panel can provide a combination of environmental, leadership, communication and personal-development experiences. 1. Participate in a Funded Residential Weekend Youth Panel members will have the opportunity to attend a funded residential weekend at a Field Studies Council field centre in the UK. For the 2026 intake, the residential weekend is scheduled to take place from Friday 6 November to Sunday 8 November 2026 at Preston Montford, Shropshire . The costs associated with the residential are covered. This residential experience provides an opportunity for members to meet other participants in person and take part in Youth Panel activities. 2. Access Training Opportunities Youth Panel members can participate in training opportunities during their time on the Panel. These include heavily subsidised Biodiversity Courses , which may be offered online and in person. Such opportunities can help young people expand their understanding of biodiversity and develop knowledge that complements their interest in nature and the environment. 3. Network With Other Young Environmentalists The Youth Panel provides an opportunity to meet other young people who are passionate about nature. Throughout their term, members will have opportunities to connect with other young naturalists and environmentalists. This can create opportunities for collaboration, knowledge exchange and building relationships with peers who share similar interests. 4. Develop Transferable Skills One of the important benefits of the Youth Panel is the opportunity to develop practical skills that can be useful beyond environmental activities. The Field Studies Council specifically identifies skills such as: Meeting skills Decision-making Influencing Collaboration Communication Participation in organisational discussions These experiences can be valuable for young people who are considering future education, volunteering, employment or leadership opportunities. 5. Create Content for Social Media and Blogs Youth Panel members can also contribute to communications activities. Members may have opportunities to create content for social media and blogs that can be shared through Field Studies Council channels as well as through their own channels. This element of the role may be particularly useful for young people interested in digital communication, journalism, social media, content creation, environmental storytelling or public engagement. 6. Represent Young People in Decision-Making Youth Panel members can represent young people s perspectives in decision-making meetings involving Field Studies Council staff and trustees. They may also have opportunities to represent the Field Studies Council at events or conferences. This provides participants with exposure to organisational decision-making and gives them an opportunity to contribute directly to conversations concerning young people and environmental education. Duration of the Youth Panel Role Members recruited during autumn 2026 are expected to serve on the Youth Panel for two years . The role is voluntary, and successful applicants will therefore need to be prepared to make a sustained commitment to the Panel throughout this period. A two-year commitment can allow members to build meaningful experience over time rather than participating in a one-off activity. It also gives participants the opportunity to develop their skills and contribute to projects throughout their period of service. Meetings and Time Commitment Youth Panel members participate in both online and in-person activities. The Panel holds an in-person residential once a year at a Field Studies Council centre. For the 2026 cohort, the annual residential is scheduled for 6–8 November 2026 at Preston Montford . Applicants are expected to confirm their availability for this date. In addition, monthly online meetings are held. These meetings alternate between weekday evenings and generally take place on Mondays, Wednesdays or Thursdays from 6:00 pm to 7:15 pm . The Field Studies Council recognises that young people may require greater flexibility at certain times of the year. Youth Panel members are expected to attend a minimum of four meetings per year and contribute to associated tasks and projects. This means applicants should consider their existing commitments, including school and other activities, before applying. Who Can Apply for the Field Studies Council Youth Panel 2026? The opportunity is open to young people who meet the specific requirements set by the Field Studies Council. Applicants must: Be aged between 16 and 18 at the time of applying . Be based in the United Kingdom . Be able to attend the in-person Youth Panel residential from Friday 6 November to Sunday 8 November 2026 at Preston Montford, Shropshire. Be able to commit approximately a couple of hours per month to meetings and related tasks. The Field Studies Council states that it welcomes applications from young people regardless of their experience or background. It also indicates that it is particularly interested in representatives from Scotland and Wales , while the Youth Panel itself is UK-wide. Country and Continent Eligibility The opportunity is restricted geographically to young people based in the United Kingdom . Therefore, applicants from the following UK nations can potentially apply, provided they meet the other requirements: England Scotland Wales Northern Ireland The source specifically highlights Scotland and Wales as areas from which the Field Studies Council is especially keen to receive representation. The eligible continent is Europe , but the actual eligibility requirement is more specific: applicants must be based in the UK . The opportunity is not presented as open to applicants from Europe generally. No Previous Experience Is Required An important feature of the opportunity is that applicants do not need to demonstrate extensive previous experience. The Field Studies Council welcomes applications from young people regardless of their experience or background. This means applicants should not assume that they need an extensive environmental, conservation or leadership record to be considered. Instead, they should use their application to explain who they are, what motivates them, what they hope to learn and what they can contribute to the Panel. What Is Required in the Application? The application consists of three main questions designed to help the Field Studies Council understand applicants, their motivations and the contribution they could make to youth engagement. Question 1: Tell Us About Yourself and Your Motivation Applicants are asked to explain something about themselves, their experiences and what motivates them to join the Field Studies Council Youth Panel. The maximum response length is 200 words . Applicants may consider discussing: Their connection with the outdoors Previous volunteering roles Areas they would like to become involved in Their motivation for representing young people Their interest in the Field Studies Council The organisation is looking for insight into the applicant as an individual and an understanding of why they want to become part of the Youth Panel. Question 2: What Do You Hope to Learn? The second question asks applicants to explain what they hope to learn from participating in the role. The maximum response length is 200 words . Applicants can consider discussing: Skills they want to develop What excites them about joining the Youth Panel How the opportunity could support their future Personal or professional development goals This is an opportunity for applicants to demonstrate that they have thought about how Youth Panel participation could contribute to their growth. Question 3: What Can You Bring to the Panel? The third question asks applicants what they could contribute to the Panel and what they hope to achieve as a Panel member. The maximum response length is 300 words . Applicants can discuss: Particular skills they possess Relevant experiences What distinguishes them from other applicants Ideas they could contribute Their goals as a Youth Panel member How they would balance Panel responsibilities with school and other commitments This question is particularly important because it allows applicants to demonstrate both their potential contribution and their understanding of the responsibilities involved in joining the Panel. Application Tips The Field Studies Council recommends preparing responses in Microsoft Word or Google Docs before copying and pasting them into the online application form. This approach can make it easier for applicants to draft, edit and review their answers before submitting the application. Applicants should ensure that their responses directly answer each question while remaining within the specified word limits. Young people should also consider demonstrating genuine motivation rather than simply listing achievements. Since the Field Studies Council welcomes applicants regardless of their experience or background, applicants can focus on their interests, perspectives, aspirations and willingness to contribute. Alternative Application Format for Applicants Who Find Online Forms Difficult The Field Studies Council provides an alternative way to respond to the application questions. Applicants who find completing online forms difficult and would prefer to talk through their answers can record their responses in video or audio format . Each question can be answered in a recording of up to three minutes . Applicants choosing this option are instructed to email their files to youth.engagement@field-studies-council.org . This provides an alternative route for young people who may communicate their ideas more effectively through spoken responses. Application and Selection Timeline The Field Studies Council has provided a clear application and selection timeline for the 2026 Youth Panel recruitment. Applications Open Applications open at midday on 14 September 2026 . Application Deadline Applications close at 9:00 pm on Sunday, 27 September 2026 . Applicants should ensure that their application is submitted before the deadline rather than waiting until the final minutes. APPLY HERE Application Outcome Applicants will hear about the outcome of their application at the start of October 2026 . Virtual Interviews Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a short virtual interview taking place on 13 or 14 October 2026 . The Field Studies Council indicates that there is flexibility for alternative arrangements. The interview is intended to allow the organisation to get to know shortlisted candidates and also give candidates the opportunity to ask questions of a current Youth Panel member. Importantly, interview questions can be shared with candidates in advance. Residential Weekend Successful applicants need to be available for the Youth Panel residential from Friday 6 November to Sunday 8 November 2026 at Preston Montford in Shropshire. The costs of the residential are covered. What Makes This Opportunity Valuable? The Field Studies Council Youth Panel provides young people with a combination of environmental engagement, youth representation and personal development. Rather than simply attending an environmental programme, participants can become part of a group that contributes to the organisation s approach to youth engagement. Members can gain insight into the workings of an environmental education charity while participating in high-level discussions concerning provision for young people. The opportunity can therefore be particularly valuable for young people who are considering future interests or careers related to: Environmental science Conservation Biodiversity Environmental education Sustainability Communications Media and content creation Youth development Advocacy Leadership Public engagement Community development A Platform for Youth Voice and Representation One of the central aspects of the Youth Panel is representation. Young people have the opportunity to provide perspectives on issues affecting youth engagement and contribute to organisational discussions. Members can represent young people at meetings involving Field Studies Council staff and trustees and may also represent the organisation at events and conferences. This creates an opportunity for participants to practise expressing ideas, listening to different perspectives, contributing constructively to discussions and communicating the interests of young people. Opportunities to Develop Through the Role The Field Studies Council notes that the Youth Panel is shaped by its members and that there will be opportunities to expand skills and experiences according to individual areas of interest. This means that the experience does not necessarily have to be limited to one particular area. Members may be able to explore interests connected to environmental education, communication, biodiversity, youth engagement, content creation, decision-making and other areas relevant to the Panel s activities. The combination of regular online meetings, annual residential activities, training opportunities and projects can provide a sustained environment for learning and participation. Important Commitment to Consider Before Applying Although the Youth Panel offers numerous development opportunities, applicants should understand that it is a two-year voluntary commitment . Successful applicants are expected to contribute time each month and attend at least four meetings per year, in addition to associated tasks and projects. They must also be able to attend the annual residential and participate in monthly online meetings. Young people should therefore consider their school schedules, extracurricular activities and other responsibilities before applying. The Field Studies Council acknowledges that participants may sometimes require flexibility during particularly busy periods. How to Apply for the Field Studies Council Youth Panel 2026 Eligible young people can apply through the official Field Studies Council application process. The application form is available through the Field Studies Council s Youth Panel application page, and applications opened on 14 September 2026 . Applicants should prepare thoughtful responses to all three questions and make sure their answers remain within the required word limits. Those who have difficulty completing the online form can instead submit video or audio responses of up to three minutes per question by email to the Youth Engagement team. Application deadline: 9:00 pm, Sunday, 27 September 2026. Visit HERE for more information about the Field Studies Council Youth Panel 2026. Key Details at a Glance Detail Information Opportunity Field Studies Council Youth Panel 2026 Organiser Field Studies Council Role type Voluntary Youth Panel membership Duration Two years Eligible age 16–18 at the time of applying Location eligibility United Kingdom Applications open 14 September 2026 Deadline 9:00 pm, 27 September 2026 Application outcome Start of October 2026 Virtual interviews 13 or 14 October 2026 Residential 6–8 November 2026 Residential location Preston Montford, Shropshire Residential costs Covered Monthly meetings Weekday evenings, generally Monday, Wednesday or Thursday, 6:00–7:15 pm Minimum meetings Four per year Training Includes heavily subsidised Biodiversity Courses Application responses Three questions Alternative format Video or audio, up to three minutes per question The details above are based on the Field Studies Council s 2026 Youth Panel application information. Conclusion The Field Studies Council Youth Panel 2026 offers young people in the United Kingdom an opportunity to play an active role in shaping youth engagement and nature education while developing valuable skills and experiences. Successful members will be able to contribute their perspectives to discussions with Field Studies Council staff and trustees, connect with other young naturalists and environmentalists, participate in training opportunities, develop transferable skills, create social media and blog content, and potentially represent young people and the Field Studies Council at events and conferences. The opportunity is open to young people aged 16 to 18 who are based in the UK , and applicants do not need to have extensive previous experience. However, they must be able to make the required commitment, including monthly meetings, associated tasks and the annual residential. Applications opened on 14 September 2026 , with the final deadline set for 9:00 pm on Sunday, 27 September 2026 . Young people interested in nature, environmental education, youth representation, communication, leadership and conservation should consider preparing their applications early and using the application questions to clearly communicate their motivation, learning goals and potential contribution to the Panel.
