title: NASA Ames STEM Engagement & Mission Experience Internship 2027: Hands-On NASA Internship for Undergraduate and Graduate Students in California
summary: The NASA Ames STEM Engagement Mission Experience Internship offers students an opportunity to gain hands-on experience at one of NASA’s major research centers while exploring the wide range of scientific, technological, educational, operational, and mission-support activities that contribute to NASA’s work. Based at NASA Ames Research Center in California , this internship is designed for students who want to understand NASA from a broader, center-wide perspective rather than focusing exclusively on one scientific or engineering discipline. Interns will work with the NASA Ames Office of STEM Engagement (OSTEM) and contribute to activities that connect students and mentors with NASA’s people, facilities, research, educational resources, and career pathways. The opportunity is particularly interesting because it welcomes students from a wide range of academic backgrounds . While STEM students can benefit from exposure to different NASA research areas, students studying education, communications, public relations, business, project management, design, digital media, and related fields may also contribute valuable skills. NASA describes OSTEM internships as short-term, hands-on opportunities through which students work on real NASA projects under the guidance of NASA mentors. NASA also states that internships can be available to both STEM and non-STEM majors. About the NASA Ames STEM Engagement Mission Experience Internship The NASA Ames STEM Engagement Mission Experience Internship is an educational internship designed to provide students with an unusual opportunity to see how a multidisciplinary NASA research center operates. Rather than assigning the intern to a narrowly defined technical research project, the internship provides exposure to different parts of NASA Ames. Students can learn about: NASA research programs Scientists and engineers STEM education and engagement Mission-support activities Research facilities Career pathways Program management Communications Educational events Student engagement initiatives Behind-the-scenes facility experiences The intern will work with the Office of STEM Engagement at NASA Ames , helping develop meaningful experiences for students and mentors. This makes the internship especially suitable for students who are curious about NASA as an organization and want to understand how different disciplines work together to support a major scientific and aerospace institution.Internship Location The internship is based at: NASA Ames Research Center California, United States The opportunity is described as fully on-site , meaning selected interns are expected to work physically at NASA Ames rather than remotely. Students should therefore consider their ability to be present at the NASA Ames facility for the duration of the internship when applying. Full-Time and Part-Time Internship Options One of the notable features of this opportunity is its flexibility. The internship is available on a: Full-time basis Part-time basis Applicants are expected to indicate their preferred arrangement in their application response. This can make the opportunity particularly useful for students who have different academic schedules or availability during the internship period. However, applicants should carefully consider the practical requirements of a fully on-site internship, including their ability to be physically present at NASA Ames. What Will the Intern Do? The internship provides exposure to a broad range of STEM engagement and mission-related activities. The intern will primarily work with the Ames Office of STEM Engagement and help support programs that connect students and mentors with NASA. 1. Support Behind-the-Scenes NASA Facility Tours One of the central components of the internship involves helping coordinate behind-the-scenes tours and learning experiences at NASA Ames research facilities . The intern may assist with: Coordinating tour schedules Organizing logistics Communicating with participants Preparing background information Developing learning materials Helping ensure that participants have meaningful educational experiences This can give the intern firsthand insight into how educational experiences are organized within a complex research institution. 2. Support STEM Engagement Events The intern may assist with STEM engagement activities and events organized by NASA Ames. Potential responsibilities include: Supporting student programs Assisting with STEM events Helping coordinate special initiatives Communicating with participants Supporting event logistics Working with organizations and teams across NASA Ames These activities can help students develop practical experience in event coordination and STEM outreach. 3. Learn About NASA Research Areas NASA Ames is a multidisciplinary research environment. The intern will have opportunities to learn about different areas of research taking place at the center and understand how these areas contribute to NASA s broader mission. This can be particularly valuable for students who want to explore NASA beyond a single technical discipline. Rather than limiting their experience to one research field, students can gain a broader understanding of the types of work performed at NASA Ames. 4. Translate Technical Information for Student Audiences Another potential responsibility is helping make technical information easier for students and other audiences to understand. The intern may contribute to: Educational resources Background materials Briefing documents Guides Digital content Informational materials STEM engagement resources This is especially relevant for students interested in science communication, education, public relations, digital media, communications, or outreach. The ability to take complex information and communicate it clearly to a general audience is an important professional skill. Interaction With NASA Professionals The internship may provide opportunities to interact with professionals working at NASA Ames, including: Scientists Engineers Researchers Program managers Mission-support professionals STEM educators Communications professionals Other NASA personnel Through these interactions, students can learn how different academic and professional disciplines contribute to NASA s missions. This can also help interns better understand the range of careers available within a large research and aerospace organization. Additional Activities Depending on the student s interests, academic background, skills, and the needs of the program, the internship may include additional activities. These can include: STEM Engagement Supporting: Student programs Educational events STEM engagement initiatives Special NASA Ames projects Content Development Creating or assisting with: Informational resources Briefings Guides Digital content Educational materials Career pathway resources Event Planning Helping with: Event organization Scheduling Participant communications Logistics Coordination between different NASA Ames organizations Participant Experience The intern may help document participant experiences and identify ways that future STEM engagement activities could be improved. New STEM Engagement Ideas Students may also be encouraged to contribute ideas for new approaches to introducing students and educators to: NASA research NASA careers Educational opportunities Scientific disciplines Engineering Technology Mission-support careers Who Should Apply? The opportunity is intentionally designed to attract students from a wide range of academic disciplines . Applicants do not need to be experts in every scientific field represented at NASA Ames. Instead, the project emphasizes qualities such as: Curiosity Initiative Organization Communication Willingness to learn Collaboration Interest in NASA Ability to work with others NASA s broader OSTEM program also states that it offers internships to non-STEM majors , meaning students do not necessarily have to be studying science or engineering to find suitable NASA internship opportunities. STEM Students The internship may be particularly valuable for students studying STEM subjects who want to understand NASA beyond a single technical discipline. STEM students can potentially use the experience to: Explore different NASA research areas Meet professionals from different disciplines Understand how research supports NASA missions Learn about STEM careers Develop professional communication skills Expand their professional network Gain experience in a major research environment Students may also discover areas of NASA work that they had not previously considered. Students Interested in STEM Education The internship can also be relevant to students considering careers in science or STEM education . Students interested in education can gain exposure to: NASA research Real-world scientific environments STEM professionals Educational programming STEM outreach Student engagement STEM career pathways This can help future educators develop a better understanding of how classroom concepts connect to real-world research and NASA missions. Non-STEM Students One of the most important aspects of this opportunity is that students from non-STEM disciplines may also bring valuable skills. Potentially relevant academic backgrounds include: Education Communications Public relations Business Project management Design Digital media Related disciplines For example, a communications student could contribute to content development and participant communication, while a project-management student could contribute to event coordination and logistics. Therefore, students should not automatically assume that NASA opportunities are restricted to engineering, physics, computer science, or other traditional STEM disciplines. NASA confirms that its OSTEM program includes opportunities for non-STEM majors. Internship Learning Objectives By the conclusion of the internship, the student is expected to have developed several important professional and academic competencies. 1. Understanding NASA Ames The student should develop a broader understanding of: NASA Ames Research Center Its research capabilities Its facilities Its people Its multidisciplinary environment Its role within NASA This broader exposure can help students understand how a large research institution operates. 2. Educational Experience Coordination Students can gain practical experience in coordinating: Educational activities Tours Events Student experiences STEM engagement programs This can strengthen their ability to work within a professional environment involving multiple stakeholders. 3. Professional Communication The internship is expected to strengthen communication skills through interaction with: Students Educators NASA professionals Researchers Engineers Program managers Other participants Communication may take place through meetings, written materials, participant communications, briefings, and educational resources. 4. Organization and Project Management Students can develop practical skills in: Planning Scheduling Coordination Organization Event logistics Project support Time management These skills can be useful regardless of the student s eventual career path. 5. Collaboration Because the internship involves working with different organizations and professionals across NASA Ames, students can gain experience collaborating in a multidisciplinary environment. This can help them understand how people with different academic and professional backgrounds work together toward common objectives. 6. Understanding NASA Career Pathways Another important objective is helping students understand the variety of careers that contribute to NASA missions. These may extend beyond traditional scientific and engineering positions to include areas such as: Education Communications Program management Administration Digital media Public relations Mission support Research Technology This broader perspective can help students identify career pathways they may not have previously considered. Professional Networking Opportunities The internship can provide opportunities for students to interact with NASA professionals. Networking with scientists, engineers, researchers, program managers, and other professionals can help students: Learn about different career paths Understand professional expectations Ask questions about NASA careers Build professional relationships Gain insight into research environments Better understand how different disciplines contribute to missions For students considering a future career in science, technology, education, communications, or mission support, this exposure can be valuable. What Makes This Internship Different? Many internships focus heavily on a single research project, technical discipline, or specialized skill. This NASA Ames opportunity is different because it emphasizes a center-wide perspective . Instead of concentrating exclusively on one research area, the intern can gain exposure to: NASA research STEM engagement Educational programming Facilities Scientists Engineers Program managers Mission-support professionals Communications Career pathways This makes the opportunity especially attractive for students who are still exploring which area of NASA or STEM they might eventually pursue. NASA OSTEM Internship Context The opportunity falls under NASA s Office of STEM Engagement (OSTEM) internship structure. NASA explains that OSTEM internships are paid, hands-on opportunities for college-level students to contribute to NASA projects under the guidance of NASA mentors. The agency offers three internship sessions annually. NASA s current published schedule lists the following OSTEM deadlines: Spring 2027: September 14, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time Summer 2027: February 26, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time Fall 2027: May 21, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time Important Deadline Note The specific NASA Ames project description provided for this article does not state a separate project-specific deadline or internship session . Therefore, applicants should verify the current session and deadline shown in the NASA application system for Project ID 025677 before submitting an application. If the project is listed under the Spring 2027 OSTEM cycle, the current NASA deadline is September 14, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET . NASA Internship Eligibility Requirements Although the individual project description says internships are available to undergraduate and graduate students aged 16 and above, NASA s current official OSTEM eligibility requirements provide additional requirements. Applicants must generally: Be a U.S. citizen Have a cumulative 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale Be a full-time or part-time college student from undergraduate through graduate level Be at least 16 years old at the time of application Be enrolled in a degree-granting program at a U.S. Department of Education-accredited college or university Be pursuing a course of study aligned with NASA s needs NASA also states that letters of recommendation are not required as part of the OSTEM internship application. Because the project description itself does not list every general NASA eligibility requirement, applicants should check the official NASA internship system and current project listing before applying. Is This Internship Open to International Students? This is an important consideration for international applicants. The standard NASA OSTEM internship program requires applicants to be U.S. citizens . NASA s current FAQ explicitly states this requirement. NASA does have an International Internship (I²) program , but NASA currently states that the International Internship program is not being offered at this time . NASA s international internship information also lists specific countries that have participating agreements when the program is active. Ghana is not among the currently listed participating countries . Therefore, an international student should not assume that they can apply to this NASA Ames OSTEM internship simply because the project description says undergraduate and graduate students . The citizenship and institutional eligibility requirements of the applicable NASA internship program must be satisfied. Funding and Internship Stipend NASA states that the majority of OSTEM interns receive a stipend award , with the amount based on academic level and session duration. However, the project description provided does not specify the exact stipend amount for Project 025677 . Applicants should therefore avoid assuming a particular dollar amount until the official NASA internship listing or offer specifies it. Housing and Transportation Applicants should also plan carefully for the practical costs associated with an on-site internship. NASA states that interns are responsible for making their own housing arrangements and paying for their housing. NASA does not provide housing, although resources may be available to help interns identify options. Because this NASA Ames opportunity is fully on-site, selected students should consider: Housing in the NASA Ames area Transportation to and from the center Local living expenses Food Personal expenses Any costs not covered by the internship stipend How to Prepare a Strong Application Students interested in Project 025677 should focus on demonstrating that they can contribute to STEM engagement while learning from NASA s multidisciplinary environment. 1. title: AfricaLics PhD Visiting Fellowship Programme 2027: Fully Supported 3-Month Research Fellowship in South Africa for African PhD Students
summary: The AfricaLics PhD Visiting Fellowship Programme (VFP) 2027 Cohort is now inviting applications from eligible PhD students enrolled at universities in African countries for an opportunity to strengthen their research, academic skills, dissertation quality and professional networks in the field of Innovation and Development (I D) . The 2027 programme combines online academic activities, research training, mentorship and a three-month study visit at the University of Johannesburg (UJ) in South Africa . The study visit is scheduled for 6 September to 3 December 2027 , with additional online activities before and after the physical residency. The fellowship is particularly relevant to doctoral researchers examining how innovation, technology, learning, institutions and competence-building interact with economic, social or environmentally sustainable development in Africa. Successful fellows will receive access to an international research environment, academic and research training, specialist mentoring, accommodation, return international airfare, a living-cost stipend of approximately US$600 per month , and support for programme-related activities. About the AfricaLics PhD Visiting Fellowship Programme The AfricaLics Visiting Fellowship Programme was established to strengthen the research capabilities of African PhD students working in Innovation and Development studies. The programme was established in 2015 with financial support from the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida) . Since its establishment, African PhD students from low- and lower-middle-income countries have participated in the programme and received research training and mentorship. The 2027 cohort continues this objective by bringing selected doctoral researchers into an intensive academic environment involving: Online preparatory activities Academic writing training Research training Paper presentation opportunities Individual and joint mentoring Interaction with researchers at the University of Johannesburg A three-month research stay in Johannesburg Face-to-face meetings Dissertation development Academic networking Post-fellowship alumni engagement The programme is intended to complement, rather than replace, the doctoral student s existing PhD programme at their home university. AfricaLics also confirms that the programme aims to strengthen students academic and research qualifications, improve the quality of their dissertations and prepare them for future careers in academia, the private sector, government and policymaking. What Is Innovation and Development Research? The AfricaLics programme focuses on the intersection between innovation and development . Innovation is understood broadly. It can involve new inventions, but it can also involve the adoption, diffusion and use of technologies that are new to a particular user or context. Innovation can also involve: New products New production processes New ways of organising activities New approaches to doing things Technology adoption Learning and competence-building Social innovation Technological innovation Institutional and organisational change Innovation and Development studies therefore examine how technological and social innovation interact with economic, social and environmental development. This makes the fellowship multidisciplinary. Applicants may come from backgrounds such as: Economics Sociology Political Science Science and Technology Policy Geography History Development Studies Science Technology Engineering Mathematics Manufacturing However, STEM and manufacturing-related research should have a relevant social-science perspective and connect to the broader relationship between innovation and development. Research Areas Covered by the Programme AfricaLics recognises a broad range of research areas at the intersection of innovation and development. Potential areas include: Energy Sustainable development Sustainable transformation Health Gender Agriculture Manufacturing Work organisation Big data The Fourth Industrial Revolution Technology and innovation policy Economic development Social development Environmental sustainability The programme is therefore not restricted to researchers whose PhD is formally titled Innovation and Development. The key consideration is whether the doctoral research addresses an important relationship between innovation and economic, social or environmentally sustainable development. AfricaLics Research Coordination Areas for 2027 For the 2027 cohort, particular encouragement is given to PhD students whose research relates to one or more of the four AfricaLics Research Coordination Areas (RCAs) . 1. STI Measurement in Africa This area focuses on science, technology and innovation measurement in African contexts. Research may examine how innovation and technological capabilities are measured, understood and used to inform development policy and decision-making. 2. Global Value Chains, Innovation and Industrialization This research area examines innovation, industrial development and the role of African economies within global value chains. Researchers may investigate issues surrounding: Industrialisation Production networks Technology upgrading Firm-level innovation Competitiveness Global production systems 3. Innovating Resilience This area focuses on inclusive agricultural innovation and climate resilience in Sub-Saharan Africa. It is particularly relevant to researchers examining how innovation can contribute to: Agricultural resilience Climate adaptation Inclusive development Food systems Rural development Sustainable agriculture 4. Innovation and Sustainable Energy Transition in Africa Known as i-SET Africa , this area focuses on innovation and the transition toward sustainable energy systems across Africa. Researchers examining energy innovation, clean energy technologies, energy policy, sustainability and related development questions may find a strong connection with this research area. The four RCAs are explicitly highlighted in the 2027 call as areas in which applicants are particularly encouraged to conduct research. Fellowship Structure The AfricaLics VFP is not simply a three-month study-abroad opportunity. It is a longer programme involving activities before, during and after the physical study visit. The 2027 cohort is expected to begin with online activities during the first half of February 2027 . The programme will then include the three-month study visit at the University of Johannesburg from: 6 September – 3 December 2027 After the Johannesburg study period, fellows will participate in additional online activities in December 2027 and early 2028. This structure is designed to make the fellowship an integrated component of the student s PhD rather than an isolated research trip. Online Academic Activities Before and around the study visit, fellows participate in online activities designed to strengthen their academic and research capabilities. The programme includes training in academic writing and research. Three short online courses are highlighted in the 2027 programme: How to Write an Academic Journal Article How to Do Systematic Literature Reviews Additional writing and research skills activities Fellows will also have opportunities to participate in paper presentation seminars. Each visiting fellow can present and participate in up to five paper presentation seminars , including a presentation during the AfricaLics PhD Academy 2027, which is expected to take place in April 2027. These activities can help doctoral students improve their ability to communicate their research to academic audiences and receive constructive feedback before completing their dissertations or publishing their work. Three-Month Study Visit at the University of Johannesburg One of the central components of the programme is the three-month research stay at the University of Johannesburg in South Africa . The study visit is scheduled for: 6 September – 3 December 2027 During this period, fellows will be exposed to an international research environment focused on Innovation and Development, including transformative innovation processes and the Fourth Industrial Revolution. The study visit is designed to give students dedicated time away from their normal duties to focus on their doctoral research. During the residency, students can work on areas such as: Consolidating their research Analysing fieldwork data Improving theoretical arguments Developing dissertation chapters Writing academic articles Refining research questions Presenting their research Receiving feedback Connecting with other doctoral researchers Engaging with experienced scholars The University of Johannesburg s research environment therefore forms an important part of the fellowship experience. Mentorship from AfricaLics and Globelics Scholars A major feature of the programme is its mentorship component. Each fellow will be matched with one or two scholars whose expertise corresponds to the student s research area.
